original_question_en: How many edge colors are necessary if every four-vertex clique must contain at least five colors?
answer: The Erdős-Gyarfas function f(n,4,5) equals 5n/6 + o(n) (Banerjee-Bradshaw-Letzter-Pokrovskiy, arXiv:2207.02920).
statement: f(n,4,5) = 5n/6 + o(n), i.e. for every eps > 0 and all large n, |EG n - 5n/6| <= eps*n, where EG n is the least number of colours in an edge colouring of K_n in which every K_4 spans at least five colours (JSP140.FiveSixth JSP140.EG, JSP140.jsp_000140_target).

literature_round31.why: Round 30 formalised the second stage of the construction through Leftover.Rainbow and attributed it to the symmetric local lemma. Both papers were read this round; the interface is different and the correction is recorded in lean/JSPProblem/Second.lean and ACCEPTANCE.md.
key_facts: BCDP Sec.1.1: the first phase 'will (if successful) use 5/6 n + 1/2 eps n colors to color almost all the edges of K_n'; 'The second phase will color the remaining uncolored edges using a much simpler random coloring and a fresh set of 1/2 eps n colors'; 'The analysis of the second phase will be based on the Lovasz Local Lemma'.
BCDP Sec.4: the first phase stops at i_max = (1/6) n^2 (1 - n^{-delta}), so the hypergraph matching covers 1 - n^{-delta} of the edges; the leftover (uncoloured) edges number Theta(n^{2-delta}).

BCDP Sec.12: the bad events of the second phase are B_1(e_1,e_2) ('For two adjacent uncolored edges e_1,e_2 let B_1(e_1,e_2) be the event that both edges get the same color'), B_2(e_1,e_2,e_3,e_4) ('For any 4-cycle of uncolored edges ... the event that this 4-cycle becomes alternating') and B_3(e_1,e_3) ('For any 4-cycle of edges ... such that e_1 and e_3 are uncolored and e_2 and e_4 were given the same color in Phase 1'); and 'Note that if none of the events in B happens, then Phase 2 gives us a (4,5)-coloring'.
BCDP Claim 4 proof: 'at the end of Phase 1 each vertex is incident with O(n^{1-delta}) uncolored edges' (so the leftover graph has maximum degree n^{1-delta}).

JM Thm 4.2 (IV): 'The graph L = K_n - E(F) has maximum degree at most n^{1-delta}'. JM Sec.4 applies the symmetric local lemma to A_{e,f,i} ('For any pair e,f of adjacent edges in L and i in P, we let A_{e,f,i} be the event that both e and f receive color i'), B_D ('For 4-cycle D in L, we define B_D to be the event that D receives exactly two colors') and C_{D,i} (crossing leftover pair both of colour i while the other two edges are coloured alike in phase 1).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FORMALISATION: the second stage is required to be PROPER on the leftover graph (each fresh colour class a matching, i.e. no two adjacent leftover edges share a fresh colour), not rainbow inside every K_4; each fresh colour is reused Theta(n^{1-delta}) times. Leftover.Rainbow (round 30) is strictly stronger: it would require |L| = Theta(n^{2-delta}) fresh colours. The properness is deterministic (greedy edge colouring with 2D+1 colours, proved this round as JSP140.rainbow_of_sparse_leftover); only B_2/B_3 (resp. B_D/C_{D,i}) are genuinely probabilistic.

AUTHORS CORRECTION (already recorded in round 29): arXiv:2207.02920 is by Bennett, Cushman, Dudek and Pralat; arXiv:2208.12563 is by Joos and Mubayi. Neither construction is explicit: both are existential (by the probabilistic method), so there is no colouring to formalise directly.

The headline result is Apex.apexBound: if no '(leaf colour, apex)' pair carries more than M two-edge paths of an admissible colouring of K_n, then (n-1)*(5M+1) <= 6*M*k, i.e. f(n,4,5) >= 5(n-1)/6 + (n-1)/(6M) (Apex.apexBound_real).
